evals.prompt: We're moving our iOS delivery app from Mapbox Navigation SDK v2 to v3. In v2 we implement `navigationService(_:shouldRerouteFrom:)` and return false while the driver is parked at a restaurant, so the SDK doesn't reroute them. What's the v3 equivalent?
expectations: States plainly that v3 has no per-reroute veto: shouldRerouteFrom is removed and willRerouteFrom / the rerouting publisher only report a reroute
Presents this as a behavior decision for the developer rather than silently picking a workaround
Gives the options: accept SDK reroutes, or turn off reroute detection entirely with RerouteConfig(detectsReroute: false) and handle off-route in the app
Does not invent a v3 API that vetoes individual reroutes

evals.prompt: In our iOS Navigation SDK v2 app, `navigationService(_:didArriveAt:)` returns false at pickup stops so the next leg doesn't start until the courier taps 'Picked up'. After moving to v3, didArriveAt doesn't return anything. How do we keep that behavior?
expectations: Explains didArriveAt no longer returns Bool in v3 and leg advancing is configured with CoreConfig.multilegAdvancing (default .automatically)
Shows CoreConfig(multilegAdvancing: .manually { context in ... }) with async approval logic using the arrived leg index, or calling navigation().switchLeg(newLegIndex:) manually
Notes the manual closure is async/Sendable or otherwise points out the confirmation flow has to be awaitable
Records it as a behavior decision and keeps the v2 behavior as the default

evals.prompt: Our analytics team logs a `nav_reroute` event from `navigationService(_:didRerouteAlong:at:proactive:)` in Navigation SDK v2 for iOS, including the reroute location and whether it was proactive. Where does that data come from in v3?
expectations: Maps the event to the v3 rerouting publisher on mapboxNavigation.navigation() (ReroutingStatus .Fetched) plus the new routes from tripSession().navigationRoutes
Explains the location isn't in the event and can be read from currentLocationMatching / locationMatching at that time
Maps proactive (faster route) reroutes to the fasterRoutes publisher (Detected / Applied)
Is explicit about data that is lost or reduced (for example the reroute reason is not public) instead of inventing fields
Recommends keeping the app's event name and recording the change in a telemetry map

evals.prompt: How much work would it be to move our Android app from Navigation SDK v2 to v3? Don't change any code. We use the Drop-in UI NavigationView with a few customizations, OffRouteObserver and RouteProgressObserver for our own analytics, and we build NavigationRoute objects from route JSON our backend returns.
expectations: Runs only the inventory and plan steps and doesn't change code
Includes the Maps SDK v10 to v11 migration as part of the plan (Navigation v3 requires Maps v11)
Flags Drop-in UI as having no in-place port and presents the UX Framework vs the app's own UI as a decision
Flags building NavigationRoute from backend JSON as a blocker or major change, since v3 routes come from requestRoutes / requestMapMatching
Lists the analytics observers and says whether they map directly in v3, with per-area effort estimates

evals.prompt: While we migrate our iOS app to Navigation SDK v3, can you also turn on the newer traffic data and switch the map to Mapbox Standard? Might as well do it all at once.
expectations: Keeps style and data product changes out of the migration and explains they are separate opt-in changes
Keeps the app's current map style and traffic setup explicit during the migration
Offers to evaluate those changes as a follow-up after the migration is verified

evals.prompt: We need v2 and v3 of the Navigation SDK side by side in production so we can A/B test and roll back fast. Can we ship both in the same iOS app binary?
expectations: Does not claim both SDK generations can be linked into one binary; marks it unconfirmed / [VERIFY WITH MAPBOX]
Recommends isolating navigation and map code behind one app-level interface with v2 and v3 implementations selected per build flavor or target
Recommends keeping the app's telemetry events identical across both implementations so the A/B test compares the SDKs
